acceptance.description: Current Electron product/design contracts and the exact integrated document set are registered and independently reviewed; user approval and matching handoffs are recorded before implementation.
The reviewed monorepo/runtime/state/UI architecture, Electron main/preload/renderer/preview boundaries, app-owned OpenCode sidecar, and required SDK/UI probes have reproducible evidence.
PRD acceptance groups AC-01–18 and integrated scenarios work with verified failure and recovery semantics.
Required automated/manual safety and quality evidence passes, including desktop lifecycle/E2E, with fresh independent code and UI reviews.

A locked, reproducible local Electron desktop build succeeds for macOS and Windows on their respective platforms; output, source revision, runtime/toolchain, artifact hash, and launch instructions are recorded.
Local redacted monitoring, diagnostics, recovery and personal-use measurement are implemented and exercised inside the desktop app without external telemetry, with operational-drill evidence.
The pinned OpenCode client synthetic transport probe validates public types and observed request/failure behavior without network access or user data.

A bridge-owned, side-effect-free single-read runtime-info boundary validates unknown SDK responses, returns minimal metadata or fixed redacted failure outcomes, and is exercised through the pinned client synthetic probe; it does not establish live host readiness or compatibility.

The installed Electron app owns its window, packaged renderer, and exact app-launched OpenCode v2 `serve` sidecar lifecycle through a typed/narrow preload API. Renderer and preview have no general Node, shell, filesystem, child-process, or sidecar-credential access. Packaged lifecycle evidence passes independently on macOS and Windows.

integrity.scope: Token aliases, component references and light/dark design system integrity

install.scope: Frozen-lockfile workspace install; may change local dependency/store state and contact the configured registry when cache is insufficient; clean-install claims require a separately recorded clean starting state

lint.scope: Actual lint and module-boundary targets for all inventoried workspace projects

format.scope: Formatting checks for all projects owning formatter-supported source

typecheck.scope: Actual TypeScript checks for all inventoried workspace projects

tests.scope: Actual uncached unit and integration targets for every inventoried product project

e2e.scope: Actual browser end-to-end integrated flows and permission/error UI using synthetic fixtures

boundaries.scope: Resolved module/import graph and negative fixtures for desktop shell, renderer, preview and bridge separation; inspect emitted desktop and renderer bundles for forbidden dependencies and secrets.

operational-drills.scope: Historical synthetic local-bridge fixture only: redaction allowlist, loopback bridge loss, owned synthetic child effect-then-crash, temporary marker/checksum recovery model, and missed/paused/duplicate schedule model. Partial AC-4 evidence only; not AC-6 production diagnostics, journal, durable recovery, DB migration, rollback, or scheduler evidence.

hooks.scope: Lifecycle-hook fixture behavior and repository hook applicability evidence

build.scope: Actual uncached production builds for the inventoried desktop shell, renderer, bridge and packages.

sdk-client-probe.scope: Pinned @opencode/client public type boundary and synthetic fetch success/failure responses passed through the shared bridge validator; no network or real service lifecycle

runtime-info-boundary.scope: Pure bridge-owned unknown-input validation, one-read outcome mapping, and redaction tests; no sockets or persistent data

desktop-app-test.scope: Selected host/client admission and lifecycle tests using an owned disposable OpenCode sidecar; include exact server identity, readiness/authentication, event-gap handling, and process cleanup without user configuration

desktop-e2e-macos.scope: Development app E2E on macOS plus sender/frame/payload admission, navigation denial, privilege absence, preview isolation, sidecar readiness, disconnect/reconnect visibility, and owned-process lifecycle assertions.

desktop-e2e-windows.scope: Equivalent development app E2E on Windows with sender/frame/payload admission, navigation denial, privilege absence, preview isolation, sidecar readiness, disconnect/reconnect visibility, and owned-process lifecycle assertions.

desktop-build.scope: Build and hash the local macOS personal-use desktop artifact; no publication or signing. Cross-build output is not Windows runtime evidence.

desktop-build-windows.scope: Build and hash the local Windows personal-use desktop artifact on Windows; no publication or signing. Record the actual runner OS.

desktop-packaged-e2e.scope: On the exact packaged macOS app and OpenCode sidecar, assert sidecar identity/readiness and the minimal client flow; reject malformed renderer messages/navigation/popups; inspect privilege absence and preview isolation; inject startup failure, crash, timeout, service collision, disconnect, close/quit/restart; observe exact child reaping; bind app and sidecar hashes to evidence.

desktop-packaged-e2e-windows.scope: On Windows, run the exact packaged app and OpenCode sidecar; verify identity/readiness and the minimal client flow; reject malformed renderer messages/navigation/popups; inspect privilege absence and preview isolation; inject startup failure, crash, timeout, service collision, disconnect, close/quit/restart; observe exact child reaping; bind app and sidecar hashes. Match the macOS assertions or document an independently reviewed platform-specific equivalent.

desktop-bundle-inspection-macos.scope: Inspect the packaged macOS renderer for Node built-ins, secrets, bridge-only code, OpenCode server code/credentials and unsafe APIs; bind report to exact app and sidecar hashes and build evidence.

desktop-bundle-inspection-windows.scope: Inspect the packaged Windows renderer for Node built-ins, secrets, bridge-only code, OpenCode server code/credentials and unsafe APIs; bind report to exact app and sidecar hashes and build evidence.

desktop-operations-recovery.scope: Planned Electron-app operations evidence on controlled synthetic state: local redacted health/diagnostics, durable recovery, backup/export verification, migration and rollback failure/success behavior, and missed/paused/duplicate schedule handling. Must record actual app and data effects, recovery outcomes, and cleanup. Persistent-data cases remain held until storage location and retention are confirmed; this planned target is not implemented yet.

decision_register.statement: The product is an installed Electron desktop app for macOS and Windows.
decision_register.source: Explicit user confirmations in the project conversation: macOS + Windows, followed by Electron selection on 2026-09-28.
decision_register.impact: Architecture, packaging, security, and runtime verification must cover both operating systems independently.
decision_register.resolution: Electron is the selected shell; actual per-OS package and sidecar behavior still requires evidence.

decision_register.statement: The Electron app owns and supervises an OpenCode v2 `serve` sidecar.
decision_register.source: Explicit user direction in the project conversation that OpenCode server runs as an app-owned sidecar.
decision_register.impact: Do not use browser loopback or a synthetic bridge as desktop sidecar evidence; do not attach to an ambient service.
decision_register.resolution: Electron main starts and supervises the exact packaged child; it keeps client credentials outside renderer and preview.

decision_register.statement: Use Electron as the desktop host.
decision_register.source: Explicit user selection in the project conversation on 2026-09-28: "electron으로 진행".
decision_register.impact: Electron-specific host, renderer isolation, sidecar lifecycle, packaging, and per-OS evidence govern implementation.
decision_register.resolution: Electron is selected. The focused desktop-app-bootstrap milestone is revision 20; its exact document-set packet r1 is approved and recorded in that run. Only the bounded synthetic-data probes and bootstrap described there may proceed; full-product and persistent-data decisions remain separately gated.

decision_register.statement: Select the persistent local location and separation strategy for app-owned user data.
decision_register.source: Not yet explicitly selected by the user; identified as unresolved in the current full-product plan.
decision_register.impact: Database, local objects, backups, privacy, export/import, and recovery must not assume a path or migrate existing data before this decision.

decision_register.statement: Select retention and deletion behavior for persistent conversation, evidence, and diagnostic records.
decision_register.source: Not yet explicitly selected by the user; identified as unresolved in the current full-product plan.
decision_register.impact: Persistence-dependent implementation and lifecycle tests must not infer retention defaults or claim deletion completeness.
